chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, who said:

It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What has come regarding fasting on Wednesday?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the Fire on Wednesday, so He made fasting on it obligatory to seek refuge by it from the Fire.'
ai.seo_question: Why is fasting on Wednesday considered significant in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi attributes the obligation of Wednesday fasting to Imam Ali, linking it to the creation of Hellfire on that day as a means of seeking refuge. While often cited in Shia tradition as a recommended or obligatory act of devotion, it reflects the broader theological concept of associating specific days with divine attributes or events to enhance spiritual mindfulness.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Hammad, from Hareyz who said,

‘It was said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What has come regarding the Fasting during the Wednesday?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created the Fire on the day of Wednesday, thus its Fasting is Obligated in order to seek Refuge by it, from the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz who has said the following: “

Someone asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about fasting on Wednesday. The Imam said, ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, “Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, created hellfire on Wednesday; for this reason there is fasting to seek refuge thereby from the fire.’””
